name: Chablis Premier Cru
terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards. The Grand Crus usually sit mid-slope and higher, with the best sun and drainage.

notes: Chablis's cool climate gives Chardonnay more acidity and less fruit than warmer regions do.
Racy, green-apple acidity is its trademark, and the style is crisper and steelier than the rest of Burgundy.
Chablis was traditionally aged in old, neutral barrels that added no oak flavor.
Some Chablis has an earthy, wet stone flavor that grows with age before mellowing into delicate honeyed notes.
Grand cru Chablis can often age well over 15 years, and many premiers crus at least 10.

blurb.text: The premier cru mention of the Chablis appellation, for white wine from Chardonnay alone. Its climats are on the best-exposed slopes, the historic ones on the right bank of the Serein. Labels can add the climat's name.
